name: GM Arnold Denker National Tournament of High School State Champions
value: 2026 prizes: Scholarships 1st $5,000, 2nd $4,000, 3rd $3,000, 4th $2,000, 5th $1,000; cash prizes 1st $800, 2nd $500, 3rd $400, 4th $300, 5th $200; Ursula Foster 15 and Under award $1,000; Joanne Haskel (Under 2000) award $100
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted. For 2026, state nomination forms were due to US Chess by June 1 and the tournament ran August 3 to 6, 2026 in Grand Rapids, MI.
apply: Qualify as your state's representative through the method your state chess affiliate chooses (usually a state championship section for grades 9 to 12); the affiliate submits the nomination to US Chess.
eligibility: One representative per state: a resident of that state, enrolled in grades 9 to 12, and 19 or younger on September 1 of the tournament year.
notes: Free event. The US Chess Trust $5,000 first-place scholarship may be used at any school of higher learning on proof of enrollment. Entry depends on winning state selection.

name: USA Brain Bee National Championship
value: 2026 prizes: 1st $1,500, 2nd $1,000, 3rd $500; the national winner represents the USA at the International Brain Bee World Championship
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted; the 2026 championship was held April 25, 2026 at UC Irvine. Students must first win a local chapter Brain Bee.
apply: Win a local (chapter) Brain Bee neuroscience competition, then register for the national championship.
eligibility: Ages 13 to 19 at the time of the competition, currently or formerly enrolled in an accredited US high school, and a winner of a local Brain Bee. Students may compete at nationals only once.
notes: The 2026 national championship had a $400 registration fee.

name: Stulberg International String Competition
value: 2026 prizes: Gold Medal $10,000, Silver Medal $7,000, Bronze Medal $5,000, Bach Prize $2,000; $1,000 stipends for the other nine semifinalists
deadline: Monday, February 1, 2027 (11:59 p.m. EST)
apply: Apply online through the competition's Acceptd portal with a video audition (concerto with piano or orchestra, recorded within 12 months of the deadline, max 20 minutes).
eligibility: Violinists, violists, cellists and double bassists age 19 or under as of January 1, 2027. Current students of the 2027 judges are ineligible.
notes: Application fee was $150 (credit card only). Twelve semifinalists perform live in Kalamazoo, Michigan in May. Full 2027 guidelines were marked coming soon on stulberg.org.

name: FBA Civics Essay Contest
value: Scholarships: First place $1,500, Second place $1,250, Third place $750
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 contest is closed and the new prompt will be posted in January 2027.
apply: Write an essay (max 1,000 words) on the annual prompt and submit it with the entry form through the online form.
eligibility: High school students in grades 9 to 12 in public, private, parochial and charter schools, and home-schooled students of equivalent grade, in the United States and its Territories.
notes: Judged on understanding of constitutional principles, clarity, grammar and composition, and citations.

name: Regions Riding Forward Scholarship Contest
value: Four quarterly contests, each awarding four $8,000 scholarships (two written essay winners and two video essay winners), paid to the winner's college
deadline: 2026 quarterly contests: Q3 closes September 30, 2026 and Q4 (October 1 to December 31) closes December 31, 2026, at 11:59:59 PM Central Time
apply: Submit a written essay (500 words max) or a video essay (3 minutes max) about a person you know personally in your community who inspired you in an extraordinary way.
eligibility: Legal U.S. residents of AL, AR, FL, GA, IA, IL, IN, KY, LA, MS, MO, NC, SC, TN or TX, age 16 or older, with a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0; high school seniors are eligible if they begin college no later than the 2027-2028 academic year. No Regions banking relationship required.
notes: Judged by an independent panel on inspiration (50), creativity and originality (25) and quality (25); no public vote or random draw. Entries must be created without AI. A person may win only one quarterly prize.

name: OG&E Positive Energy Scholarship
value: Three scholarships of up to $60,000 each ($15,000 per year for up to four years)
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; applications reopen in fall 2026. The 2026 deadline was January 15, 2026.
apply: Apply online through OGE.com/scholarships when the application reopens.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors whose primary residence is in the OG&E service area (Oklahoma or western Arkansas), planning to attend college in Oklahoma or Arkansas in one of 23 approved STEM or business majors, with an unweighted GPA of 3.25 or higher.
notes: Renewable for up to four consecutive years with an unweighted GPA of 2.75 or higher. The scholarships page also says applicants must be OG&E customers.

name: Alliant Energy Innovation Scholarship
value: $1,000 each, up to 25 awards, one-time and non-renewable
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted; Alliant lists an annual window of Dec. 2 to Feb. 3.
apply: Apply online through Scholarship America with an official transcript and a 350-word essay.
eligibility: High school seniors age 24 or under who are U.S. residents in the Alliant Energy service territory (Iowa and Wisconsin), dependent children of current customers in good standing (Interstate Power and Light or Wisconsin Power and Light), with a 2.5 to 4.0 GPA, enrolling for the first time full time in a STEM field or craft/skilled trade at an accredited two- or four-year school in Iowa or Wisconsin.
notes: Scholarship America page states financial need is not considered. Selection weighs field of study, leadership and community service, GPA and the essay.

name: Edison Scholars Program
value: $50,000 each (distributed over four years), 30 awards annually
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the program page says the 2027 program opens this fall. The prior cycle ran November 6, 2025 to January 22, 2026.
apply: Apply online at edisonscholars.com; the top 50 finalists submit a short video about their community impact plans using STEM.
eligibility: High school seniors living in Southern California Edison's service area with a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0, demonstrated financial need, and plans to enroll full time at a four-year accredited college in an eligible STEM major.
notes: Merit and financial need are both weighed. Dependents of Edison International and SCE employees and retirees are not eligible. Recipients may apply for a paid SCE summer internship.

name: Dominion Energy Educational Equity Scholarship Program
value: Up to 20 awards of $5,000 for two-year programs and at least 40 awards of $10,000 for four-year degrees; renewable up to three additional years
deadline: 2027 cycle not yet posted; the official page lists the most recent close as March 12 at 4 p.m. ET.
apply: Apply through Scholarship America with an official transcript, the first two pages of the most recent IRS Form 1040, and one online recommendation.
eligibility: High school seniors, graduates or current undergraduates residing in CT, MD, NC, SC, VA or WV with a minimum 3.0 GPA, planning full-time undergraduate study at an accredited institution.
notes: 80% of awards use a combination of need and merit; 20% are merit only. Renewal requires a 2.5 cumulative GPA and continued state residency.

name: Unitil STEM Scholarships
value: $5,000 each, five scholarships (plus one for a Unitil employee's child), for the first year of undergraduate study
deadline: 2027-28 cycle not yet posted; the 2026-2027 application has closed.
apply: Submit the application with an official high school transcript, a recommendation from a STEM teacher or principal, and an essay on career objectives and merit.
eligibility: High school seniors who live in and attend school in eligible Unitil service-territory towns in New Hampshire, Massachusetts and Maine and who declare a STEM major.
notes: Committees weigh academic merit, financial need, other scholarships awarded, activities and work hours.

name: Robert E. Evans Scholarship
value: Amount varies each year based on number of recipients
deadline: Next cycle opens January 4, 2027; the stated deadline is March 31.
apply: Apply online during the application window (opens early January).
eligibility: High school seniors in Ohio, West Virginia, Kentucky, Virginia, Maryland or Washington, D.C. with a GPA of 3.5 or higher, pursuing a four-year degree in business, education, engineering, liberal arts, math, science or technology.
notes: Applicants must demonstrate financial need, with preference to higher need.

name: Rotary Club of Los Angeles Scholarships
value: $10,000 per scholarship, 25 scholarships annually
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 deadline was March 2, 2026.
apply: Apply online through the club's Kaleidoscope application portal.
eligibility: College-bound high school seniors graduating from schools in Los Angeles County with a record of academic excellence and outstanding commitment to community service.
notes: Prioritizes high-need, high-performing students; recipients typically have 3.7 to 4.0 unweighted GPAs (not a stated minimum).

name: Rotary Four-Way Test Speech Contest (District 7390)
value: District finals: $1,250 (1st), $750 (2nd), $500 (3rd), $250 each (4th and 5th)
deadline: 2026-27 cycle: club winners must be submitted by March 13, 2027; mid-level round March 27, 2027; finals April 17, 2027.
apply: Compete in a local Rotary club contest; club winners are entered online by the club (one student per school district advances).
eligibility: Students in grades 10 to 12 at public, private or charter high schools or homeschooled in Adams, Cumberland, Dauphin, Lancaster, Lebanon, Perry and York Counties, PA.
notes: Students choose their own topic and apply the four principles of the Four-Way Test.

name: High School Student Four-Way Test Speech Contest (District 5930)
value: District level: $1,500 (1st), $1,000 (2nd), $750 (3rd), $100 all others; club and area prizes also awarded
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted; in 2026 club contests were due March 14, area contests March 25, and the District Championship was April 11, 2026.
apply: Compete at a Rotary club contest; top two advance to area, then district.
eligibility: Open to all high school students in Rotary District 5930 (South Texas).
notes: Five to seven minute speech applying the Four-Way Test; judged on content (50%), organization (30%) and delivery (20%).

provider: Rotary District 5340 (San Diego and Imperial Valley)
name: Rotary Four-Way Test Speech Contest (District 5340)
value: District finals: $1,000 grand prize, $750 runner-up, $500 other finalists; awards also at club, subregional and regional levels
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted; in 2026 club contests ran January to February and district finals were April 15.
apply: Be selected by a teacher and sponsored by a District 5340 Rotary club, then advance through club, subregional and regional rounds.
eligibility: High school students ages 14 to 18 residing in Rotary District 5340 (San Diego and Imperial Valley) who have not previously won first place.
notes: Five to seven minute original speech; no props.

name: Rotary 4-Way Test Speech Contest (District 5790)
value: 2026 prizes: $1,000 (1st), $800 (2nd), $600 (3rd), $400 (4th), two honorable mentions of $300
deadline: 2027 contest dates not yet posted.
apply: Compete at a Rotary club contest; each club submits one winner to advance through regional and district rounds.
eligibility: High school students in grades 9 to 12 (homeschoolers welcome) in the North Texas area of District 5790 who have not competed at the district level in a prior year.
notes: Topic: What the Four-Way Test Means to Me; five minute speech, no scripts or props.

name: William J. Schulz Memorial Essay Contest for College-Bound High School Seniors
value: First through tenth place awards from $3,500 down to $300, plus optional honorable mentions of $200 each (2026 contest)
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 deadline was June 1, 2026.
apply: Submit the essay through FFRF's online application form; essays must include links or footnotes for quotes and citations.
eligibility: High school seniors who will attend a North American college or university in the fall after graduation (2026 contest: spring 2026 graduates).
notes: Topic changes yearly (2026: a favorite freethought or humanist hero). AI writing assistance is not allowed; grammar and spell check are permitted.

name: Bennington Young Creators Awards (Young Artists, Innovators, Musicians and Scientists)
value: Cash prizes in each discipline: First $2,000, Second $1,000, Third $500, Distinguished $250. If enrolling at Bennington: First Place full tuition for four years, Distinguished half tuition for four years, Finalists $25,000 per year for four years.
deadline: Submissions accepted September 1 at 9:00 AM ET through November 1 at 11:59 PM ET; winners announced in spring.
apply: Submit one entry per discipline online; grade 12 students submit through the Common App or Coalition Application. A sponsoring teacher or mentor must approve each entry.
eligibility: Students in grades 9 to 12 worldwide; graduated students are not eligible.
notes: Separate from the Young Writers Awards. Free to enter. AI is prohibited for the Artists, Musicians and Scientists awards and permitted only under set conditions for Innovators. Tuition scholarships apply only if the winner enrolls at Bennington.

name: Sejong Writing Competition: Sijo (Pre-college Division)
value: Pre-college division: First $500, Second $400, Third $300; honorable mentions $50 each
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 deadline was February 28, 2026 (11:59 PM CT).
apply: Write one sijo (Korean poetic form) in English on any topic and submit it through the Sejong Cultural Society website without your name on the entry.
eligibility: Residents of the United States and Canada age 18 and younger (pre-college division), regardless of ethnic background.
notes: The essay category was discontinued starting in 2026; only the sijo category continues. AI use must be disclosed.

name: Federal Junior Duck Stamp Conservation and Design Contest
value: National: First place $1,000, Second $500, Third $200; Conservation Message winner $200 (2026 contest). National art winner also gets a trip to the First Day of Sale ceremony.
deadline: Entries go to your state contest by the state's deadline; check the state coordinator list for the current date.
apply: Complete the entry form (grades 7 to 12 also need the reference form) and mail the artwork to your state coordinator. State Best of Show winners advance to the national contest.
eligibility: Students in kindergarten through grade 12 who are U.S. citizens, resident aliens or nationals; U.S. citizens at schools abroad enter through their state of legal residence. One entry per student; the previous year's national winner may not enter.
notes: Prize amounts come from the 2026 national results release.

name: Brower Youth Awards
value: $3,000 cash prize, a co-produced short film about the recipient's work, and a leadership trip with flight, meals and lodging
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 deadline was March 31, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time.
apply: Complete the online application with a personal photo. Semifinalists submit a letter of support (not from a parent) and do a video call with the selection panel.
eligibility: Young environmental leaders ages 13 to 22 as of the deadline living in North America, including Mexico, Canada and U.S. territories.

name: BMI Composer Awards (Student Composer Awards)
value: Awards totaling $20,000 each year, including the Ellen Taaffe Zwilich Prize for the top work and the Carlos Surinach Prize for the youngest winner
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 cycle measured age as of February 15, 2026. Sign up on the BMI Foundation site for deadline notices.
apply: Submit an anonymized score and an audio rendering (MIDI is fine) of one original, unpublished composition through the application portal when it opens.
eligibility: Composers under age 28 who live in the U.S. or its territories or are citizens of a Western Hemisphere country; no more than two prior BMI Composer Awards.
notes: Open to a wide age range, so high-school entrants compete with college and graduate composers.

provider: Ronald Reagan Presidential Foundation and Institute
name: Ronald Reagan Debate Series (Great Communicator Debate Series)
value: $50,000 in college scholarships at the National Championship; first place $10,000, runner-up $7,500
deadline: 2026-27 regional invitationals: November 14, 2026 (Irvine, CA); February 20, 2027 (Richmond, VA); March 6, 2027 (Dallas, TX); April 3 to 10, 2027 and May 1 to 8, 2027 (multiple sites); June 5, 2027 (online). More dates may be added.
apply: Register for a regional invitational through Tabroom.com; top regional finishers advance to the National Championship at the Reagan Library.
eligibility: High school students in grades 9 to 12 in the United States.
notes: 2027 topic concerns disaster preparedness and response roles of state, local and federal government. Entry fees and regional prize amounts are not stated on the official page.

provider: Ronald Reagan Presidential Foundation and Institute
name: GE-Reagan Foundation Scholarship Program
value: $10,000 per year, renewable for up to three additional years (up to $40,000)
deadline: 2027 cycle dates not yet posted; the prior cycle opened October 13, 2025 and closed January 5, 2026 at noon CST.
apply: Online application (administered by Kaleidoscope) with activities, community service, work experience, a leadership essay and a goals statement; semifinalists submit transcripts.
eligibility: U.S. citizens who are current high school seniors with at least a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale, planning full-time study at an accredited four-year U.S. college.
notes: Selection centers on leadership, drive, integrity and citizenship; applicants are first considered on merit, but financial information is one component of the evaluation.

provider: Ronald Reagan Presidential Foundation and Institute
name: GE Aerospace-Reagan Workforce Readiness Scholarship
value: Up to $10,000 per year; at least 10 scholars selected each year
deadline: 2027 cycle not yet posted; applications for 2025-2026 are closed. Register on the foundation site for 2027 notices.
apply: Apply online through the program administrator, Kaleidoscope, when the 2027 cycle opens.
eligibility: High school seniors entering technical training, industry certifications, skilled-trade training, two-year degrees or other workforce-aligned programs, with a focus on aerospace, manufacturing, robotics and related industries.
notes: 25% of awards are reserved for students from military households. Citizenship and GPA rules are not stated on the pages read.

name: Hispanic Heritage Youth Awards
value: Up to $4,000 per recipient toward educational goals; Gold, Silver and Bronze honors in each category plus one National Youth Award recipient per category
deadline: November 1, 2026 at 11:59:59 PM PST (application and document uploads)
apply: Apply online at the Youth Awards portal with the application form, one letter of recommendation and a school transcript.
eligibility: High school students graduating in spring 2027 who live in the U.S. or its territories, have at least a 3.0 unweighted GPA (or 7.5 on a 10.0 scale) and will enroll in an accredited institution in 2027-28.
notes: Categories include Community Service, Green, Engineering, Entrepreneurship, Technology and Journalism and Media (more may be announced). Recipients must attend a virtual celebration, and national awardees an in-person ceremony. Confirm any heritage requirement in the application.

name: ACT-SO (Afro-Academic, Cultural, Technological and Scientific Olympics)
value: National gold, silver and bronze medals plus college scholarship opportunities from national sponsors (amounts not stated)
deadline: Local competitions run February to April; local gold medalists advance to the national competition held in July at the NAACP convention. 2027 national dates not yet posted.
apply: Enroll in a local ACT-SO program through an NAACP branch or youth council, compete locally, and advance as a gold medalist.
eligibility: U.S. citizens in grades 9 to 12 who are amateurs in their category; 33 categories across humanities, performing arts, visual arts, culinary arts and STEM.
notes: Participation runs through local NAACP units; check your local chapter for its schedule.

name: Young American Creative Patriotic Art Contest (and 3-D Patriotic Art Contest)
value: 2-D contest national awards total $37,000: First $15,000, Second $7,500, Third $3,500, 4th and 5th $1,500, 6th and 7th $1,000, 8th to 13th $500. 3-D contest national awards total $5,500.
deadline: March 31: student entries due to a participating sponsoring VFW Auxiliary
apply: Submit original artwork to a local participating VFW Auxiliary; state first-place winners advance to national judging.
eligibility: Students in grades 9 to 12 at U.S. public, private, parochial or home schools (or overseas dependents of U.S. military or civilian personnel) who are U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents or have applied for permanent residence. Not open to foreign exchange students, students age 20 or older, or prior national winners.
notes: Digital art, photography, 3-D printed work, weapons and jewelry are not accepted.

provider: National Society Daughters of the American Revolution
name: Dr. Aura-Lee A. and James Hobbs Pittenger American History Scholarship
value: $2,000 per year for up to four years
deadline: Scholarship portal reopens November 1, 2026. The DAR FAQ lists the deadline as January 31 at 11:59 pm Hawaii Time; confirm the 2027 date when the portal opens.
apply: Apply through the DAR online scholarship portal with transcript, typed recommendation letters, and a one-page personal statement.
eligibility: Graduating high school students who are U.S. citizens and will pursue an undergraduate degree including at least 24 credit hours in American history and American government.
notes: A 3.25 GPA is required for renewal. DAR membership and chapter sponsorship are not required. Applicants may receive only one national DAR scholarship.

provider: National Society Daughters of the American Revolution
name: Lucinda Beneventi Findley History Scholarship
value: $2,000 (one-time)
deadline: Scholarship portal reopens November 1, 2026. The DAR FAQ lists the deadline as January 31 at 11:59 pm Hawaii Time; confirm the 2027 date when the portal opens.
apply: Apply through the DAR online scholarship portal with transcript, typed recommendation letters, and a one-page personal statement.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors who are U.S. citizens with at least a 3.25 GPA, an advanced interest in history, and plans to major in history at a full-time accredited U.S. college.
notes: DAR membership and chapter sponsorship are not required. Applicants may receive only one national DAR scholarship.

provider: National Society Daughters of the American Revolution
name: Richard and Elizabeth Dean Merit Scholarship
value: Two scholarships of $5,000 per year, renewable for up to four consecutive years
deadline: Scholarship portal reopens November 1, 2026. The DAR FAQ lists the deadline as January 31 at 11:59 pm Hawaii Time; confirm the 2027 date when the portal opens.
apply: Apply through the DAR online scholarship portal; winners submit official transcripts each year by July 1 to renew.
eligibility: Graduating high school students with a 4.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale (or equivalent) who will major in American Studies (American history, government, literature, art history, music or culture) at an accredited U.S. institution. DAR scholarships require U.S. citizenship.
notes: Selection is on academic merit only. Renewal requires a 3.25 GPA.

name: Jon H. Poteat Scholarship
value: $1,000; 275 awarded
deadline: Application window September 1 to May 1
apply: Log in to the NTHS member portal and apply; active members may apply once per scholarship cycle.
eligibility: Active NTHS members (career and technical education students).
notes: Requires NTHS membership through a school chapter.

name: NTHS Build Your Future Scholarship
value: $2,000; 5 awarded
deadline: Application window October 1 to April 1
apply: Apply through the NTHS member portal.
eligibility: High school seniors or postsecondary students in construction-related fields (listed among NTHS member scholarships).
notes: Requires enrollment in a construction discipline.

name: FIRST Scholarship Program (via Pearson Futures Portal)
value: Varies by provider; more than 150 colleges, universities and businesses offer scholarships to FIRST participants
deadline: Varies by provider; most applications are due between December and April of senior year.
apply: Browse and apply to individual scholarships on the Pearson Futures Portal, checking each provider's eligibility and deadline.
eligibility: Current and former FIRST program participants (FIRST LEGO League, FIRST Tech Challenge, FIRST Robotics Competition); requirements vary by scholarship.
notes: Portal listing many separate awards; split into individual records.

name: Dr. Bart Kamen Memorial FIRST Scholarship
value: Up to four awards of $10,000, renewable for up to three more years (up to $40,000)
deadline: Opens annually; exact dates are announced through FIRST newsletters and social media and on the Submittable portal. 2027 dates not yet posted.
apply: Submit the online application and supporting documents on the Kamen scholarship Submittable portal.
eligibility: High school seniors (or graduates not yet in full-time college) accepted to or applying to an accredited biomedical engineering or pre-medical program, with at least one year on a FIRST LEGO League, FIRST Tech Challenge or FIRST Robotics Competition team. U.S. citizens and international students are eligible.
notes: Selection weighs academics and character; financial need is not required but may be considered. Renewal requires annual research projects and papers in biomedical engineering or medicine.

name: National Greek Exam (NGE) Scholarship
value: $1,000, paid to the winner's institution
deadline: Application information goes to teachers of qualifying students in May; winners announced at the ACL Institute in June. 2027 dates not yet posted.
apply: Teachers of qualifying seniors receive application details in May; the NLE/NGE Scholarship Committee selects winners.
eligibility: High school seniors who earned purple or blue ribbons on upper-level National Greek Exams and commit to earning six credits of ancient or biblical Greek in their first college year.
notes: Requires taking the National Greek Exam (spring).
